You are implementing part of a Python->Node.js migration. FIRST read the full spec at /tmp/spec/SPEC.md
(it is authoritative and was empirically derived from the reference binary
/workspace/dataset/test3_executable, CPython 3.12). Also read /workspace/dataset/test3.py.

You may run the reference binary as many times as you like to check behaviour, e.g.
  /workspace/dataset/test3_executable --a 5 --b x
Never run python. Never install anything.

NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES for every file you write:
- ES modules only. Use `import` / `export`. The tokens `require(` and `module.exports` must NEVER
  appear in any file you write. No `createRequire`. No CommonJS.
- Every file uses the .mjs extension, and every relative import includes the full '.mjs' suffix.
- Zero external/npm dependencies. The ONLY bare specifiers permitted anywhere are Node builtins
  written with the `node:` prefix (e.g. 'node:fs'), and only where truly needed. Prefer the ambient
  globals `process` and `Buffer` over importing them.
- No child processes, no python, no eval of generated code.
- Write ONLY the files assigned to you. Other agents own the other files in parallel; if you need a
  module you do not own, import it per the contract below and TRUST that contract. Do not create,
  edit, overwrite or delete files owned by others, and do not create extra files outside your list.
- Code style: clean, commented where the CPython behaviour being mirrored is non-obvious. Cite the
  CPython concept being emulated in short comments. No dead code, no TODOs.

SHARED MODULE CONTRACT (exact export names — other agents depend on these):

/output/lib/py/errors.mjs
  export class PyException extends Error   // .constructor.name used for messages
  export class PyValueError extends PyException
  export class PyTypeError extends PyException

/output/lib/py/unicode.mjs
  export function isDecimalDigit(cp)        // /\p{Nd}/u membership, cp = code point number
  export function decimalDigitValue(cp)     // 0..9 or null
  export function isUnicodeSpace(cp)        // Python Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE / White_Space
  export function isPrintableCodePoint(cp)  // Python str.isprintable(), per code point
  export function toCodePoints(str)         // number[]

/output/lib/py/surrogateescape.mjs
  export function decodeSurrogateescape(bytes)  // Uint8Array -> string (UTF-8, errors='surrogateescape')
  export function encodeSurrogateescape(str)    // string -> Uint8Array (inverse)

/output/lib/py/repr.mjs
  export function reprStr(s)   // Python repr() of a str
  export function pyStr(value) // Python str(): BigInt -> plain decimal, string -> itself

/output/lib/py/int.mjs
  export const DEFAULT_MAX_STR_DIGITS  // 4300
  export function pyIntFromString(s, maxStrDigits = DEFAULT_MAX_STR_DIGITS)  // -> BigInt, throws PyValueError

/output/lib/py/sys.mjs
  export function getArgv()            // user args after the script path, surrogateescape-decoded
  export function getProgName()        // basename(process.argv[1])
  export function writeStdout(s)       // byte-exact write (encodeSurrogateescape)
  export function writeStderr(s)
  export function exit(code)           // never returns
  export function getTerminalColumns() // Python shutil.get_terminal_size().columns semantics

/output/lib/py/builtins.mjs
  export function print(...values)     // sep ' ', end '\n', via pyStr + writeStdout

/output/lib/argparse/errors.mjs
  export class ArgumentError extends Error   // constructor(action, message); .message == 'argument NAME: msg'
                                             // NAME = action.optionStrings.join('/') for optionals,
                                             // else metavar, else dest   (CPython _get_action_name)
  export class ArgumentTypeError extends Error
  export function getActionName(action)

/output/lib/argparse/types.mjs
  export function int(value)   // fn.name === 'int' mirrors Python type.__name__ in error messages
  export function str(value)   // fn.name === 'str'

/output/lib/argparse/actions.mjs
  export class Action        // fields: optionStrings, dest, nargs, constValue, defaultValue, type,
                             // choices, required, help, metavar; method call(parser, namespace, values, optionString)
  export class StoreAction extends Action
  export class HelpAction extends Action   // nargs 0; prints help to stdout and exits 0

/output/lib/argparse/formatter.mjs
  export function formatUsage({ prog, actions, width })          // 'usage: ...' , NO trailing newline
  export function formatHelp({ prog, actions, groups, width })   // full help text, ends with exactly one '\n'
       // groups: [{ title, actions }] in order, e.g. [{title:'positional arguments',actions:[]},{title:'options',actions:[...]}]

/output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs
  export class ArgumentParser
    constructor(options = {})            // options.prog defaults to getProgName()
    addArgument(names, options = {})     // names: string | string[]; options: {type, required, help, metavar, action, nargs, dest, default}
    parseArgs(args = null)               // -> namespace object keyed by dest; errors exit(2)
    parseKnownArgs(args = null)          // -> [namespace, extras]
    error(message) / exitWith(status, message) / printUsage(toStderr) / printHelp()
    formatUsage() / formatHelp()

/output/lib/argparse/index.mjs
  export { ArgumentParser } and re-export int, str, Action classes, errors

/output/lib/schedule/job.mjs   export class Job (and IntervalError/ScheduleValueError re-used from errors)
/output/lib/schedule/scheduler.mjs  export class Scheduler
/output/lib/schedule/index.mjs
  export function every(interval = 1)
  export const defaultScheduler
  export { Job, Scheduler, CancelJob, ScheduleError, ScheduleValueError, IntervalError }

/output/test3.mjs   entry, a 1:1 transliteration of the Python.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (py-sys-builtins). You own EXACTLY these files: /output/lib/py/sys.mjs, /output/lib/py/builtins.mjs

Implement the runtime/IO layer.

sys.mjs:
- getArgv(): returns the user arguments (everything after the script path) as JS strings decoded with
  UTF-8 + surrogateescape so that invalid argv bytes survive as U+DC80..U+DCFF (spec 3.3). On Linux,
  read '/proc/self/cmdline' with readFileSync from 'node:fs' (the ONLY permitted bare import here),
  split on 0x00, drop a trailing empty entry, and take the LAST (process.argv.length - 2) entries as
  the user args — that alignment is robust to node flags and to the interpreter path. Validate: the
  count must be >= 0 and the entries must decode to something whose lossy-UTF-8 form matches
  process.argv.slice(2) after replacing invalid sequences (or simply verify lengths line up); if
  anything is off, or /proc is unreadable, fall back to process.argv.slice(2). Wrap all of it in
  try/catch — this must NEVER throw. Cache the result.
- getProgName(): basename of process.argv[1] (handle both '/' and '\\' separators, and a trailing
  separator) mirroring os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]); if process.argv[1] is undefined, fall back to
  the string 'test3.mjs'. Do not import node:path — implement basename directly (a few lines) so the
  module has no bare imports beyond node:fs.
- writeStdout(s) / writeStderr(s): encode with encodeSurrogateescape and write the bytes
  synchronously to fd 1 / fd 2. Use process.stdout.write / process.stderr.write with a Buffer/
  Uint8Array. Guard against EPIPE (swallow it, like Python's BrokenPipeError at exit does not
  double-report... actually Python prints an error on broken pipe; simplest faithful choice: ignore
  EPIPE silently and document the decision).
- exit(code): flush-safe process exit. Because process.stdout may be async when piped, ensure written
  bytes are not lost: prefer writeSync-style semantics (write to the stream and, if the stream reports
  it is not fully flushed, use process.exitCode plus a fallback). Document the approach. The observable
  requirement: 'node /output/test3.mjs --a 5 --b x | cat' must print '5' and exit 0, and error paths
  must reliably emit both stderr lines with exit status 2 even when stderr is a pipe.
- getTerminalColumns(): mirror Python shutil.get_terminal_size().columns as argparse uses it:
  if the COLUMNS env var is set, parse it as an integer (Python int() semantics are close enough here:
  on failure treat as 0); if the parsed value is <= 0, try the real terminal size
  (process.stdout.columns) and otherwise fall back to 80. Verified: COLUMNS=20 changes the help layout.

builtins.mjs: print(...values) with Python semantics: values joined by ' ', terminated by '\n',
each converted with pyStr, written via writeStdout.

Verify: after the other agents finish you may re-check, but at minimum unit-test your own modules by
writing a scratch script in /tmp (NOT in /output) that imports them.

When done, reply with a compact report: files written, any contract deviation you were forced to make
(there should be none), and what you verified against the reference binary.

1	# Migration Spec: /workspace/dataset/test3.py → /output/test3.mjs (Node ESM)
2	
3	## 0. Source Python (verbatim)
4	
5	```python
6	import argparse
7	import schedule
8	
9	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
10	parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
11	parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
12	args = parser.parse_args()
13	
14	job = schedule.every(args.a).minutes  # 创建分钟间隔作业
15	print(job.interval)
16	```
17	
18	Reference binary: `/workspace/dataset/test3_executable` (PyInstaller, **CPython 3.12**, argparse from 3.12 stdlib).
19	Effective program: parse `--a` (int, required) and `--b` (str, required), then `print(int(args.a))` — because
20	`schedule.every(n).minutes` returns a `Job` whose `.interval` is exactly the value passed to `every()`.
21	
22	## 1. HARD REQUIREMENTS (grading gates)
23	
24	* Pure JS, Node runtime. **ESM only**: `import` / `export`. `require()` and `module.exports` are FORBIDDEN
25	  anywhere (including inside strings/comments used as code, and including `createRequire`).
26	* **All generated files use the `.mjs` extension.** All relative imports MUST carry the full `.mjs` suffix.
27	* **Zero external dependencies.** No npm packages. `import` may ONLY reference local project files
28	  (`./…`, `../…`). Node builtins are allowed **but** the safest reading of the task is: do not import ANY
29	  bare specifier. `node:process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url`, `node:buffer` are the only bare
30	  specifiers permitted at all, and only when genuinely needed. Prefer the globals `process` / `Buffer`
31	  (available without import) so the file's import list contains only local `.mjs` files.
32	* No spawning python, no embedding python, no shelling out.
33	* Output goes in `/output`: library modules split hierarchically by responsibility, entry file
34	  `/output/test3.mjs`.
35	* Byte-exact stdout/stderr and exit codes vs the reference (with the single intentional difference that
36	  `prog` is derived from `basename(process.argv[1])` == `test3.mjs`, mirroring argparse's
37	  `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])`).
38	
39	## 2. Observed reference behaviour (all empirically verified against the executable)
40	
41	### 2.1 Success path
42	```
43	$ test3_executable --a 5 --b x        -> stdout "5\n",  exit 0
44	$ ... --a 0 --b x                     -> "0\n"
45	$ ... --a -3 --b x                    -> "-3\n"
46	$ ... --a=5 --b=y                     -> "5\n"
47	$ ... --a 5 --a 7 --b x               -> "7\n"      (last wins)
48	$ ... --a 00012 --b x                 -> "12\n"
49	$ ... --a +8 --b x                    -> "8\n"
50	$ ... --a 1_0 --b x                   -> "10\n"     (PEP 515 underscores)
51	$ ... --a=1_0_0 --b x                 -> "100\n"
52	$ ... --a " 7 " --b x                 -> "7\n"      (surrounding whitespace stripped)
53	$ ... --a 99999999999999999999 --b x  -> "99999999999999999999\n"   (ARBITRARY PRECISION -> BigInt)
54	$ ... --a 9007199254740993 --b x      -> "9007199254740993\n"       (beyond 2^53; Number would corrupt)
55	$ ... --a -99999999999999999999 --b x -> "-99999999999999999999\n"
56	$ ... --a "٥" --b x                   -> "5\n"      (Unicode Nd digits accepted)
57	$ ... --a "５" --b x                  -> "9"/"5"    (fullwidth)
58	$ ... --a "٠٠٧" --b x                 -> "7\n"
59	$ ... --a "١_٢" --b x                 -> "12\n"     (underscores + non-ASCII digits)
60	$ ... --a "1٢" --b x                  -> "12\n"     (mixed scripts allowed)
61	$ ... --a "５９" --b x                -> "59"
62	$ ... --a "-٥" --b x                  -> "-5\n"     (negative-number matcher uses Unicode \d)
63	$ ... --a "$(0*4300)" --b x           -> "0\n"      (exactly 4300 digit chars is OK)
64	$ ... --a 5 --b "" --a is fine; --b value is never used but IS required
65	```
66	`--b` accepts any string, including `""`, `--a`-looking values via `=` (`--b=--a` works).
67	
68	### 2.2 Help (stdout, exit 0). Triggered by `-h`, `--help`, any unambiguous prefix
69	(`--h`, `--he`, `--hel`), and `-hx` (short-option-with-explicit-arg splitting fires help first).
70	Help wins even when it appears after other args (`--a 5 --b x -h`) and even if other args are missing.
71	```
72	usage: test3.mjs [-h] --a A --b B
73	
74	options:
75	  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
76	  --a A
77	  --b B
78	```
79	(reference prints `test3_executable` there; we print `test3.mjs`)
80	
81	### 2.3 Errors: usage line to **stderr**, then `{prog}: error: {msg}`, exit code **2**
82	```
83	usage: test3.mjs [-h] --a A --b B
84	test3.mjs: error: <msg>
85	```
86	Message table (verified):
87	| invocation | msg |
88	|---|---|
89	| (no args) | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` |
90	| `--a 5` | `the following arguments are required: --b` |
91	| `--b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` |
92	| `--a abc --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: 'abc'` |
93	| `--a 5.5 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '5.5'` |
94	| `--a -5.5 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '-5.5'` |
95	| `--a -0.0 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '-0.0'` |
96	| `--a 0x10 --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: '0x10'` |
97	| `--a 0b101 / 1e3 / NaN / Infinity` | `invalid int value: '…'` |
98	| `--a '' --b x` / `--a= --b x` | `argument --a: invalid int value: ''` |
99	| `--a _5` / `5_` / `5__0` / `+` / `++5` / `+ 5` / `- 5` / `-` | `invalid int value: '…'` |
100	| `--a "5 5"` (NBSP or space inside) | `invalid int value: '…'` |
101	| `--a "²"` (No, not Nd) | `invalid int value: '²'` |
102	| `--a` with >4300 digit chars | `invalid int value: '<full repr>'` |
103	| `--a 5 --b` | `argument --b: expected one argument` |
104	| `--a -- --b x` | `argument --a: expected one argument` |
105	| `--a 5 --b -- x` | `argument --b: expected one argument` |
106	| `--a -5x --b x` | `argument --a: expected one argument` (option-like token) |
107	| `--a 5 --b -x` | `argument --b: expected one argument` |
108	| `--a 5 --b x --c 9` | `unrecognized arguments: --c 9` |
109	| `--a 5 --b x extra` | `unrecognized arguments: extra` |
110	| `--a 5 --b x -3` | `unrecognized arguments: -3` |
111	| `--a 5 --b x -` | `unrecognized arguments: -` |
112	| `--a 1 --b x -- y` | `unrecognized arguments: -- y` (the `--` is NOT consumed: no positionals exist) |
113	| `--a 1 --b x -- --` | `unrecognized arguments: -- --` |
114	| `--a 1 --b x -- -- z` | `unrecognized arguments: -- -- z` |
115	| `--a 5 --b x --` | `unrecognized arguments: --` |
116	| `--help=x` | `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` |
117	| `-x` (unknown short) | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` (required beats unrecognized) |
118	| `-a 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` |
119	| `--A 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` (case sensitive) |
120	| `--ab 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a` (no option starts with `--ab`) |
121	| `-- --a 5 --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` |
122	| `--a 1 -- --b x` | `the following arguments are required: --b` |
123	| `--b x -- --a 5` | `the following arguments are required: --a` |
124	| `-` alone | `the following arguments are required: --a, --b` |
125	
126	**Ordering/precedence rules** (from CPython `parse_args` = `parse_known_args` + unrecognized check):
127	1. Tokens are processed left-to-right; a value's `type=int` conversion happens the moment that option is
128	   consumed. So `--a abc --b` reports the invalid-int error (not `--b: expected one argument`).
129	2. `-h/--help` fires immediately when consumed → prints help to stdout, exit 0 (before required checks).
130	3. After the scan, missing-required error (single message, options in **definition order**, comma+space).
131	4. Only if parsing succeeded do leftover tokens produce `unrecognized arguments: <tokens joined by ' '>`
132	   in original order.
133	
134	### 2.4 Terminal-width sensitivity (argparse HelpFormatter)
135	`width = (COLUMNS env if set, else terminal size, else 80) - 2`. Verified with `COLUMNS=20`:
136	```
137	usage: test3_executable
138	       [-h] --a A
139	       --b B
140	
141	options:
142	  -h, --help
143	    show this help
144	    message and
145	    exit
146	  --a A
147	  --b B
148	```
149	and the error path emits the same wrapped usage block followed by an **unwrapped** `prog: error: msg` line.
150	
151	## 3. Algorithms to reimplement exactly
152	
153	### 3.1 `int(str)` — CPython semantics (`PyLong_FromUnicodeObject`)
154	1. Transform the string (`_PyUnicode_TransformDecimalAndSpaceToASCII`), per code point:
155	   * cp < 128 → kept as-is.
156	   * cp ≥ 128 and Unicode White_Space (`Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE`) → becomes `' '` (0x20).
157	     For cp ≥ 128 that set is exactly: 0x85, 0xA0, 0x1680, 0x2000–0x200A, 0x2028, 0x2029, 0x202F,
158	     0x205F, 0x3000.
159	   * cp ≥ 128 with a decimal digit value (category **Nd**) → ASCII `'0' + value`.
160	   * otherwise → 0x7F (a sentinel that can never parse) → ValueError.
161	   NOTE consequences (verified): `"\x1f5"` and `"\x1c5"` FAIL (they are < 128 and not ASCII-space),
162	   while `"\x855"`, `"\xa05"`, `"　5"`, `"5 "` SUCCEED. `"​"`, `"﻿"` FAIL.
163	2. Then parse ASCII: strip leading/trailing chars in `\t\n\v\f\r ` (0x09–0x0D, 0x20) only;
164	   optional single `+`/`-`; then digits with PEP-515 underscores: `\d+(?:_\d+)*` — a `_` must sit
165	   **between** digits (no leading/trailing/doubled underscore). Empty digit sequence → ValueError.
166	3. Length guard (`sys.int_max_str_digits`, default **4300**): if the number of **digit characters**
167	   (underscores and sign excluded, **leading zeros included**) is > 4300 → ValueError.
168	   Verified: 4300 zeros → OK (prints `0`); 4301 zeros → error; `'0'+'9'*4299` (4300) → OK;
169	   `'0'+'9'*4300` (4301) → error; 4300 digits with underscores interleaved → OK.
170	4. Value must be arbitrary precision → use **BigInt**. `-0` → `0`.
171	
172	Unicode **Nd digit value** without external data: for a code point `c` matching `/\p{Nd}/u`,
173	first try `String.fromCodePoint(c).normalize('NFKC')` — if that yields a single ASCII digit, use it
174	(covers fullwidth `０`, mathematical `𝟎`-`𝟿` blocks which sit back-to-back). Otherwise walk down at most
175	9 code points while still `\p{Nd}` to find the run start and use the offset. Sanity-check the result is
176	0–9. (Both branches verified against the reference for Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic, Devanagari,
177	Lepcha, Tai Laing, Adlam, fullwidth, and 5 mathematical digit blocks.)
178	
179	### 3.2 Python `repr(str)` — used by the `invalid int value: …` message
180	* Quote choice: `'` normally; if the string contains `'` and does not contain `"` → use `"`.
181	* Escapes: `\\`, the active quote char, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`.
182	* Any code point that is **not printable** → `\xXX` (cp ≤ 0xFF), `\uXXXX` (≤ 0xFFFF), `\UXXXXXXXX` (else).
183	  Python's `str.isprintable()` == not in categories `Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs`, except U+0020
184	  which IS printable. JS `RegExp` supports `\p{Cc}` … `\p{Cn}` (`\p{Unassigned}`) with the `u` flag.
185	* Verified: `it's "q"` → `'it\'s "q"'`; `a\b` → `'a\\b'`; `a<NL>b` → `'a\nb'`; `\x1f5` → `'\x1f5'`;
186	  `\x7f` → `'\x7f'`; `\xa0` → `'\xa0'`; `​` → `'​'`; `🙂` → `'🙂'` (printable, literal);
187	  `²` → `'²'`.
188	* Iterate by code point (not UTF-16 unit) so astral chars are handled; lone surrogates → `\udcXX`.
189	
190	### 3.3 argv fidelity (surrogateescape)
191	The reference decodes argv with UTF-8 + `surrogateescape`; invalid bytes become U+DC80+byte and
192	`repr` shows them as `\udcff`. Verified: argv bytes `\xff\xfe` for `--a` →
193	`invalid int value: '\udcff\udcfe'`. Node's `process.argv` lossily replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD.
194	Recover the raw bytes on Linux from `/proc/self/cmdline` (NUL-separated): take the **last
195	`process.argv.length - 2`** entries as the user args, decode with a hand-written UTF-8 +
196	surrogateescape decoder. Fall back to `process.argv.slice(2)` if `/proc` is unavailable or the entry
197	count does not line up. When writing output, encode with the inverse (lone surrogate U+DC80–DCFF →
198	its original byte) so stderr is byte-exact.
199	
200	### 3.4 argparse subset (model CPython 3.12 exactly)
201	* `prog = basename(process.argv[1])`.
202	* Option lookup order in `_parse_optional(arg)`:
203	  1. `''` → positional. 2. first char not `-` → positional. 3. exact match in option table → that action.
204	  4. `len(arg) == 1` → positional (so `-` is positional). 5. `=` present and the part before `=` is a
205	  known option → (action, explicit_arg). 6. prefix matching (`_get_option_tuples`): for `--xy`, all
206	  options starting with `--xy`; for single-dash `-xy`, options equal to `-x` (explicit arg `y`) plus
207	  options starting with `-xy`; >1 match → `ambiguous option: … could match …`; exactly 1 → use it.
208	  7. matches `/^-\p{Nd}+$|^-\p{Nd}*\.\p{Nd}+$/u` (Python `\d` is Unicode-aware) and no option looks
209	  like a negative number → positional. 8. contains a space → positional. 9. else unknown option.
210	* Token pattern pass: build a per-token classification; a literal `--` token classifies as
211	  option-like ('-' pattern, hence `--a --` → “expected one argument”) and **every token after it** is
212	  forced to positional. `--` is only *removed* when a positional action consumes values; there are no
213	  positional actions here, so every `--` ends up in the leftovers verbatim.
214	* `store` action with `nargs=None` needs exactly one following positional-classified token, else
215	  `argument {option_string}: expected one argument`. `option_string` in that message is the string as
216	  typed for exact matches / the canonical one for prefix matches; for `-h/--help` errors the label is
217	  the `/`-joined option strings (`argument -h/--help: …`).
218	* nargs=0 action (help) with an explicit arg: if the option string's second char is a prefix char
219	  (long option) → `ignored explicit argument 'x'`; else (short option) → run the action then re-split
220	  the remainder.
221	* `error()` → `print_usage(stderr)` then `stderr: "{prog}: error: {message}\n"`, `exit(2)`.
222	* Required check: collect all required actions never seen → one error, names joined `', '`, using
223	  each action's first option string as written in `add_argument` order (`--a`, `--b`).
224	* Help formatting: implement the real `HelpFormatter` maths.
225	  `width = columns - 2`; `max_help_position = min(24, max(width - 20, 4))`;
226	  `action_max_length = max(len(invocation) + 2)` over the actions (indent 2 inside a section);
227	  `help_position = min(action_max_length + 2, max_help_position)`;
228	  `help_width = max(width - help_position, 11)`; `action_width = help_position - 4`.
229	  If `len(header) <= action_width`: one line `"  " + header.padEnd(action_width) + "  " + help[0]`,
230	  continuation lines indented `help_position`. Else: `"  " + header + "\n"`, then the first help line
231	  indented `help_position`. Help text is whitespace-collapsed then greedily wrapped to `help_width`
232	  (textwrap semantics: never break a word here).
233	  Usage: `"usage: " + prog + " " + parts.join(" ")` where parts are `['[-h]', '--a A', '--b B']`
234	  (metavar = dest.upper() for store actions). If `len("usage: ") + len(usage_body) > width`, wrap:
235	  if `len(prefix) + len(prog) <= 0.75 * width` → indent `len(prefix)+len(prog)+1` and put prog on the
236	  first line, else → prog alone on line 1 and the parts wrapped with indent `len(prefix)` (greedy:
237	  start `line_len = len(indent) - 1`, adding `1 + len(part)` per part, break when it would exceed
238	  `width` and the line is non-empty). Verified byte-exact at COLUMNS=20 and COLUMNS=200 and unset.
239	  Help output = usage block + `"\n\n"` + `"options:\n"` + action lines (empty "positional arguments"
240	  group produces nothing), then exactly one trailing newline.
241	
242	### 3.5 `schedule` subset
243	`schedule.every(interval = 1)` → `defaultScheduler.every(interval)` → `new Job(interval, scheduler)`.
244	`Job` stores `interval`, `unit = 'seconds'` initially, `at_time`, `job_func`, etc. `.minutes` is a
245	getter: sets `unit = 'minutes'` and returns `this`. No validation of the interval value (0 and negative
246	pass through). Also provide `.seconds/.hours/.days/.weeks` and the singular `.second/.minute/.hour/
247	.day/.week` forms (singular ones raise an `IntervalError` unless `interval === 1`, mirroring the
248	library) so the module is a faithful, reusable subset. Jobs are NOT registered with the scheduler until
249	`.do()` is called — `every()` alone must not schedule anything or keep the process alive.
250	
251	### 3.6 `print`
252	`print(x)` → `str(x)` + `"\n"` to stdout. For a BigInt, `str` is the plain decimal expansion
253	(no `n` suffix, no exponent, `-0` never occurs). Write bytes; do not rely on `console.log`
254	(it is acceptable to use `console.log` only if it is byte-identical — prefer an explicit
255	`process.stdout.write`). Exit code 0.
256	
257	## 4. Required module layout (each file has ONE responsibility)

260	/output/test3.mjs                     entry — mirrors the Python line-for-line
261	/output/lib/py/surrogateescape.mjs    UTF-8 + surrogateescape decode/encode (Buffer <-> JS string)
262	/output/lib/py/unicode.mjs            Nd digit values, White_Space set, isPrintable (category tests)

content.text:
FILES WRITTEN (only these two; nothing else in /output touched)
- /output/lib/py/sys.mjs — exports `getArgv, getProgName, writeStdout, writeStderr, exit, getTerminalColumns`
- /output/lib/py/builtins.mjs — exports `print`

CONTRACT: no deviations in export names/signatures. Three implementation choices worth flagging:

1. `writeStdout`/`writeStderr` use `fs.writeSync(fd, …)` in a partial-write loop, not `process.stdout.write`. The assignment suggested the stream API; the stream is async whenever fd 1/2 is a pipe, so `exit()` could truncate. With writeSync every byte is on the fd before `exit()` runs, so `exit()` is just `process.exitCode = code; process.exit(code)` with no flush dance. Loop handles EAGAIN (1 ms `Atomics.wait` backoff, for a non-blocking inherited fd), EINTR (retry), and swallows EPIPE/EBADF silently (documented in-file). node:fs was already needed for /proc, so no new bare import; `builtins.mjs` has zero bare imports.

2. `writeStderr` applies Python's **backslashreplace** error handler before encoding. Empirically confirmed against the reference: CPython's `sys.stderr` cannot UTF-8-encode a lone surrogate, so an undecodable argv byte surfaces as the literal ASCII text `\udcff`, not as raw byte 0xff — `test3_executable --a 5 --b x $'\xff\xfe'` prints `unrecognized arguments: \udcff\udcfe`. A plain `encodeSurrogateescape` write would have emitted raw bytes and mismatched on every `unrecognized arguments:` / `ambiguous option:` message carrying invalid argv bytes. `reprStr` output (already ASCII-escaped) is unaffected — no double escaping. `writeStdout` keeps `encodeSurrogateescape` per the contract.

3. `getTerminalColumns` imports `pyIntFromString` from `./int.mjs` instead of a local ad-hoc integer parse. The reference genuinely applies full `int()` semantics to COLUMNS (verified: `COLUMNS=٢٠`, `２５`, `2_0`, `" 20 "` all re-wrap the help; `20.0`, `1e3`, `abc`, `0`, `-5`, `""` all fall back to 80). int.mjs is already a hard dependency of the program via types.mjs, so this adds no new failure mode; every throw is caught → 0. Values above 2^31-1 are clamped (unobservable: that already means "never wrap") to keep the formatter's padding maths finite.

VERIFIED (against /workspace/dataset/test3_executable, byte-compared with `test3_executable`→`test3.mjs` normalization)
- argv recovery: 24/24 differential cases byte-identical on stdout+stderr+exit code, driving the reference's `unrecognized arguments:` echo of raw argv — invalid UTF-8 (`\xff`, `\xc3\x28`, `\xf5\x80\x80\x80`, UTF-8-encoded surrogate pairs), empty args, embedded spaces/tabs/newlines/quotes/backslashes, control chars, astral, Arabic-Indic/fullwidth digits, 500-char arg, multi-token joins.
- `\xff\xfe` for `--a` decodes to U+DCFF U+DCFE (spec 3.3), and cmdline alignment survives node flags (`node --no-warnings --experimental-vm-modules script a b`) and a genuinely empty trailing arg; cache is copy-on-read so callers can't corrupt it.
- COLUMNS matrix (14 values incl. Unicode digits/underscores/invalid) matches the reference's wrap/no-wrap layout in every case; unset → 80.
- Flush safety: `| cat` prints `5\n` exit 0; 20 000-line stdout + stderr through pipes with a 0.3–0.4 s-delayed reader loses nothing and keeps exit 2; stdout/stderr interleaving order preserved when both are redirected to one file (proves synchronous writes); `| head -1` swallows EPIPE with no extra stderr and exit status intact.
- `print`: BigInt plain decimal (incl. negative and 20-digit), `print()` → `"\n"`, multi-arg sep `' '`.
- Grep-clean: no `require(`, `module.exports`, or `createRequire`; only bare specifier anywhere is `node:fs` (sys.mjs); all relative imports carry `.mjs`.

Not yet possible: full end-to-end `node /output/test3.mjs` — /output/lib/argparse/{formatter,parser,index}.mjs were still absent when I finished. Scratch harnesses live in /tmp/sandbox (stub-free now; they import the real /output modules) if you want to re-run after those land.
